 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant-claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'M.V. Act') challenging the judgment and award passed by the Senior Civil Judge and ACJM,
Karkala, Udupi in MVC No.556/2021 dated 01.09.2022, seeking enhancement of the compensation.

2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
3.
The rank of the parties before the Tribunal is retained for the sake of convenience.

4. The case of the petitioner is that the petitioner filed petition under Section 166 of M.V. Act for claiming NC: 2024:KHC:20518 compensation for the injury sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

It is alleged that on 12.03.2021 at 9.30 a.m., when the petitioner was riding his two wheeler motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-20-Y-4547 along with the pillion rider one Mohan Hegde near Sarvajna Circle, at that time a Mahendra Jeeto Mini Goods Van bearing registration No.KA-19-AB-2893 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the two wheeler.
Due to which, the petitioner sustained injuries.
He was shifted to the Hospital, taken treatment as in patient and due to the injury he is suffering from disability.
He was doing coolie work and also engaged in the business of animal husbandry and selling of milk.
Due to the injury, he is unable to work properly and lost the future income.
Hence, on various heads, the petitioner claimed for the compensation.

5. In response to the summons, the respondent No.2 appeared and filed objection by denying the rash and negligent driving, age, occupation and income of the petitioner and prayed for dismissing the petition.

Mahammed Isak vs Ummar Farooq on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93090005/
2 6.

Based upon the pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
NC: 2024:KHC:20518 "1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries on 12.03.2021 at 9.30 a.m., Nakre Junction, Kukkundoor Village, due to rash and negligent driving of Mahindra Jeeto Mini Goods Van bearing Reg.No.KA-19-AB-2893 by its driver as contended?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount, if so what is the amount and from whom it is recoverable?

3. What Order or Award?"
7.
In order to prove the case of the claimants, the petitioner himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked 21 documents and on behalf of the respondents, no evidence were led.

8. After hearing the arguments, the Tribunal answered issue No.1 in the affirmative and issue No.2 in the partly affirmative and granted compensation of Rs.1,59,364/- on various heads which are as under:
1. Towards Pain and sufferings Rs.50,000-00 2.
Towards conveyance, Attendant Rs.20,000-00 charges and Nourishing Food.
3. Towards loss of income during laid up Rs.28,500-00 period NC: 2024:KHC:20518 4.
Towards loss of amenities and Rs.50,000-00 discomforts 5.
Medical expenses Rs.10,864-00 Total Rs.1,59,364-00 9.
Being aggrieved by the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant-petitioner filed this appeal.
10. The learned counsel for the appellant merely contended the Tribunal not at all considered the loss of future income due to the disability.

Though the petitioner produced disability certificate as per Ex.P.14, along with the CT Scan films and X-ray films as per Exs.P.20 and 21, the Tribunal has not considered the disability and not awarded any compensation towards the loss of future income.
Merely, the doctor was not examined by the petitioner before the Tribunal.

Therefore, it is contended that when the doctor was opined 19.44% of disability to the particular limb i.e., left lower limb, atleast 1/3rd of the disability should have taken towards the whole body, but nothing has been taken by the Tribunal.
Therefore, it is contended that the disability should be considered and enhanced the compensation.
Further it is contended that the income taken by the Tribunal is also very NC: 2024:KHC:20518 meager.
Normally, as per the notional income recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, an income of Rs.15,000/- is to be considered for the accident occurred in the year 2021.

Therefore, prayed for enhancing the same and also contended Mahammed Isak vs Ummar Farooq on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93090005/
3 that there is meager amount awarded towards pain and suffering, conveyance and food and nourishment charges, loss of amenities.

11. The learned counsel also relied upon the judgment of the High Court of Jharkhand in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Arun Kumar reported in LAWS (JHAR)-2022-3-91.
12.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Arun Kumar reported in LAWS (JHAR)-2022-3-91
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent- Insurer seriously objected the petition and contended that the doctor who was issued disability certificate has not been examined.

Therefore,
question of granting of any compensation towards the loss of future disability does not arise.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation.
Hence, prayed for dismissing the appeal.

In support of his case, the learned counsel for respondent relied upon the judgment of the NC: 2024:KHC:20518 Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and Another reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
13.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and Another reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Having heard the arguments and on perusal of the records, the points that arise for my consideration are:
"1) Whether in view of non examination of the doctor who has issued the disability certificate, the Court bound to accept the evidence of the petitioner and to grant compensation on the head of loss of future income due to disability?
2) Whether the appellant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?
3) If so, what order?
14.

It is worth to mention in respect of accident due to rash and negligent driver,
there is no dispute except the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

The learned counsel for the appellant has contended due to some inadvertent, the petitioner not able to examine the doctor who issued the disability certificate and as per Ex.P.14, 19.44% of disability towards the lower limb, therefore, even in the absence of evidence of the doctor, the Court can accept the NC: 2024:KHC:20518 disability certificate and can award the compensation on the ground of loss of future income due to the disability.

15. Learned counsel for the appellant relied upon the judgment of the Jharkhand High Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. stated supra, where the Jharkhand High Court has held at paragraph No.10 which is as under:
"10.
It is a settled principle of Law that the proceedings in a claim Tribunal are not required to strictly follow the provisions of C.P.C. and the Evidence Act.

Therefore,
the permanent disability certificate which has been marked as Exhibit-3 without objection cannot be discarded simply because the doctor issuing the certificate has not be examined."

Mahammed Isak vs Ummar Farooq on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93090005/
4 16.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar stated supra, where the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held at paragraph No.18 which is as under:
"18.

The Tribunal should also act with caution, if it proposed to accept the expert evidence of doctors who did not treat the injured but who give `ready to use'
disability certificates, without proper medical assessment.

There are several instances of unscrupulous doctors who without treating the injured, readily giving NC:
2024:KHC:20518 liberal disability certificates to help the claimants.
But where the disability certificates are given by duly constituted Medical Boards, they may be accepted subject to evidence regarding the genuineness of such certificates.
The Tribunal may invariably make it a point to require the evidence of the Doctor who treated the injured or who assessed the permanent disability.

Mere production of a disability certificate or Discharge Certificate will not be proof of the extent of disability stated therein unless the Doctor who treated the claimant or who medically examined and assessed the extent of disability of claimant, is tendered for cross- examination with reference to the certificate.

If the Tribunal is not satisfied with the medical evidence produced by the claimant, it can constitute a Medical Board (from a panel maintained by it in consultation with reputed local Hospitals/Medical Colleges)
and refer the claimant to such Medical Board for assessment of the disability."
17.

On perusal of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it is categorically held that when the doctor who issued the disability certificate is not examined, then the court cannot bound to accept the disability certificate as the doctor who issued the disability certificate was not the doctor who has treated the patient.
Therefore, mere marking a document in the evidence of the petitioner even if it is not objected by the other side, that is not a proof.
It is well settled that mere - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:20518 production of document and marking the documents is not a proof, until it is proved in accordance with law.
The maker of the document i.e., the doctor who issued the disability certificate not examined before the Court.
Such being the case, question of granting any loss of compensation towards the loss of future income on the disability cannot be granted.
Therefore, the contention of the appellant counsel cannot be acceptable as the Court is bound to accept and grant a compensation even if the doctor not examined by the claimant.
Therefore, the question of enhancing or computing any compensation towards the loss of future income due to the disability does not arises.
Therefore, the Ex.P.14 cannot be acceptable and no compensation can be awarded in this case towards the loss of future income.

18. As regard to the other heads, the Tribunal considered the injury and awarded Rs.50,000/-
towards pain and suffering.
The petitioner sustained fracture of lower limb, admitted as in patient for 8 days and subsequently he had further treatment.

Such being the case, I am of the view, the petitioner is entitled for some more enhancement in the head of Mahammed Isak vs Ummar Farooq on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93090005/
5 - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:20518 pain and suffering, where, I proposed to award Rs.60,000/- towards the pain and suffering instead of Rs.50,000/-
19.
As regards to the conveyance, Rs.20,000/- is awarded which is appropriate and proper, no need to interfere.
20. As per the notional income recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, an income of Rs.15,000/- is to be considered for the accident occurred in the year 2021.
Such being the case, I proposed to take Rs.15,000/- as income instead of Rs.14,250/- which is considered by the Tribunal.
21. The loss of income during the laid up period is granted Rs.28,500/- for only two months.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries, therefore, the laid up period must be calculated atleast for three months.
Therefore, Rs.15,000/- x 3, it comes to Rs.45,000/-.
Hence, I proposed to award Rs.45,000/- from instead of Rs.28,500/- awarded by the Tribunal.

22. As regards to the loss of amenities and discomforts, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.50,000/-,
there is no need to - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:20518 enhance.
The medical expenses awarded based upon the evidence of the doctor and the same is retained.

23. Thus in all, this Court has awarded the compensation under various heads as follows:
1. Towards Pain and Sufferings Rs.60,000-00 2.
Towards conveyance, Attendant Rs.20,000-00 charges and Nourishing Food.
3. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.45,000-00 4. Loss of amenities and discomforts Rs.50,000-00 5.
Medical expenses Rs.10,864-00 Total Rs.1,85,864-00 Rounded off to Rs.1,86,000-00
Hence, the appellant-claimant is entitled for a total enhanced compensation of Rs.1,86,000/- as against Rs.1,59,364/-.

24. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER Mahammed Isak vs Ummar Farooq on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93090005/
